title: NIST CFReDS Hacking Case: all 31 official questions
instructions: Answer all 31 official questions using only supplied evidence and the public case context. Do not read private references, published answers, saved scores or other systems' answers.
Return {schema_version:2, case_id, answers:[{question_id,status,answer}]}. Status is answered, unknown or unanswered. False and zero are claims, not synonyms for unknown.
Public schemas define typed answer roles. Required fields describe a complete response; omit unsupported fields and explain limitations outside answer. Never guess to fill a field.

Keep supporting observations, evidence paths, tools, reasoning, and qualifications in top-level submission appendices or the report, outside answer. Extras inside answer are extra assertions under the deterministic rubric.

Lists are unordered multisets. Preserve distinct observations and meaningful duplicates. Submit only requested items; do not pad with alternatives. An unresolved reference is reported separately, not silently counted wrong.

String matching ignores case and repeated whitespace only unless a question publishes another rule. Preserve filenames, full paths, account identities and unusual characters. Use single Windows path separators; do not invent a drive prefix.

Timestamps require an explicit source-supported UTC offset. Do not infer local display timezone from this profile or shift timestamps to match another source. Printed precision and event meaning must remain explicit in the evidence appendix.
An answer score is deterministic agreement with a versioned reference. It is separate from proof verification, extraction completeness, attribution, and investigation completeness.
The public source obscures a suspect name with equals signs to avoid indexing; the official scenario says those signs do not occur in the evidence. The wording is preserved in the prompts.

Where a public list_rules subset count is declared, submit exactly that many distinct supported examples. The accepted pool is private; extra or repeated submissions are not a shortcut to full credit.

For Q3 and Q8, this contract interprets the published local-time display in the contemporaneous time zone addressed by Q4. Submit a source-supported explicit offset; the public profile does not disclose that offset. This is a declared comparison convention, not proof of the original display configuration.

For Q31, report the antivirus result as a Boolean and document the actual scanner, version/signature date, scope, detections and failures outside answer. Boolean agreement does not verify that the examination occurred or that every infection was found.

Every scored answer leaf declares x-claim-requirement. This checks compatibility with specific reviewed claim roles, not English entailment or answer completeness. A currently unsupported stronger role remains unsupported; do not replace it with a generic string-valued observation.

questions.prompt: What is the image hash? Does the acquisition and verification hash match?

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Algorithm of a reviewed logical/acquisition image-digest role; a comparison result requires the separate equality relation.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: A fixed reviewed image-digest role or a same-algorithm digest comparison over the bound logical-image subject. Keep algorithm/digest source association explicit.

digest.description: Hexadecimal digest of the reconstructed acquired media, not the compressed container or an individual segment.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Digest recomputed over logical media bytes, not container or segment bytes.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: A completed logical-media hash calculation tied to the examined image subject. A retained acquisition checksum is not required merely to report a computed digest; it is required for the separate comparison assertion.

acquisition_verification_match.description: Agreement of acquisition and verification media digests; identify their observations separately in the evidence appendix.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Equality of acquisition and recomputed logical-image digests for the same algorithm and subject; not original authenticity.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Both bound digests and the approved equality relation.

questions.prompt: An internet search for vendor name/model of NIC cards by MAC address can be used to find out which network interface was used. In the above answer, the first 3 hex characters of the MAC address report the vendor of the card. Which NIC card was used during the installation and set-up for LOOK@LAN?

network_card.description: Network-interface vendor identity at the precision of the reference answer. Put the supported model and prefix-association evidence outside answer.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Network interface identified as used during the referenced installation/setup; not merely a matching vendor or a configured interface.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Source-scoped setup observations and a justified link from their network identity to the identified interface. Vendor-prefix lookup alone does not establish use during setup.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Program recorded as installed, not merely mentioned by an application artifact.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: An installation record plus separately inspectable justification for the requested capability. The installation claim alone does not prove hacking, intent or execution.

questions.prompt: Ethereal, a popular “sniffing” program that can be used to intercept wired and wireless internet packets was also found to be installed. When TCP packets are collected and re-assembled, the default save directory is that users \My Documents directory. What is the name of the file that contains the intercepted data?

file_name.description: Filename of the captured/intercepted data; provide the evidence path separately.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: name of the source containing captured traffic observations
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Source observations must carry this exact reviewed role, native value type and bound source subject/exhibit. Question relevance and evidence scope remain separately inspectable; a differently typed fact or arbitrary annotation cannot supply this field.

questions.prompt: Viewing the file in a text format reveals much information about who and what was intercepted. What type of wireless computer was the victim (person who had his internet surfing recorded) using?

computer_type.description: Device/platform type supported by the captured data; no stronger identification from an agent string alone.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Device/platform type supported by captured traffic under an explicit interpretation; not physical-device identity from an unverified User-Agent string.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: A reviewed interpretation of captured protocol/client evidence with spoofability and scope stated. Raw User-Agent text alone is not this stronger semantic role.

questions.prompt: What websites was the victim accessing?

items.description: Website host/domain (without scheme/path) or explicitly named web-service product. For a service, use its product name and keep provider qualifiers, URLs and reconstruction evidence outside answer.

x-claim-requirement.meaning: Host or URL observed in captured HTTP traffic; not personal attribution or proof of successful browsing.
x-claim-requirement.evidence_needed: Traffic from the referenced capture source must support the requested website/service identification. Context and any service-name interpretation stay separately inspectable; arbitrary browser history is insufficient.
